top_categories.workout_context: 10,890ft of climbing means repeated surges above threshold. VO2max work is how you survive the fifth climb, not just the first.
Sierra Nevada Límite Gran Fondo's mixed terrain forces constant power changes. Accelerate over rises and out of corners, settle on the open road, and repeat for 73 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Sierra Nevada Límite Gran Fondo's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before May.
147ft/mi means long efforts at or near FTP on every climb. If your threshold cracks at minute 15, you'll walk the rest.
At Sierra Nevada Límite Gran Fondo, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
10,890ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At Sierra Nevada Límite Gran Fondo, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Sierra Nevada Límite Gran Fondo. Train it until it feels boring.
Base fitness for Sierra Nevada Límite Gran Fondo. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.
73 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
Short, max efforts are unavoidable. Punchy climbs, gap closures, attacks on mixed terrain. If you haven't trained them, you'll crack.
Low-cadence force work for 10,890ft of climbing. The slow, grinding ascents where you can't spin—you push.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 40–60g carbs/hour for Sierra Nevada Límite Gran Fondo’s 73 miles. Front-load calories in the first half. One bottle per hour minimum, more in heat.
race_overlay.altitude: Sierra Nevada Límite Gran Fondo with 10,890ft of climbing, much of it above 8,000ft demands altitude preparation. Arrive 5–7 days early for acclimatization. Expect 5–15% power reduction at altitude. Increase iron intake 4 weeks out. Hydrate aggressively — altitude increases fluid loss by 20–40%. Precipitation: Moderate, with possible flurries at elevation.
race_overlay.terrain: Highly technical terrain at Sierra Nevada Límite Gran Fondo demands practice on similar surfaces. Ride mixed terrain at race-day cadence weekly. Practice cornering, descending, and power delivery on unstable surfaces. Test tires and pressure in comparable conditions before race week rather than guessing from a generic time-loss claim.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, Road Specific, and Race Simulation to prepare you for 73 miles of mixed terrain in Cenes de la Vega, Granada, Spain.
